holes_found.description: COVERAGE FAILURE on patch 1 propagation: the polar-offset value 0.74° → 0.66° was propagated through detail_evidence (4 occurrences) and through tldr_evidence + tldr_verdict (3 occurrences), but NOT through the summary-table `finding` field (still reads "Polaris is 0.74° from true pole; 'excess' is within known offset.") nor through the verdict-panel `detail_verdict_text` (still reads "Polaris is 0.74° from true pole; the claimed +0.27° 'excess' is within the known offset range."). The curmudgeon procedure (§1) explicitly flags summary-table-vs-detail inconsistency as a defender-exploitable hole: readers who never click through to expand the detail panel see only the finding row, which now numerically disagrees with the patched detail. A defender pointing this out ("your summary says 0.74°, your detail says 0.66°, your astrometry is sloppy") does not refute the analytical claim but discredits review care. The 0.74° value is also factually outdated per c3 hole 1 itself — the correct epoch-2026.0 value is 0.66° (90° − 89.34°). This is the same scope-coverage failure the decider would have caught with a pre-commit "every 0.74 occurrence with polar or pole nearby is patched" sweep; the commit message even self-documents the scope ("(4 detail_evidence + 2 tldr)") which by inclusion-of-tldr signals awareness that propagation should cross field boundaries — `finding` + `detail_verdict_text` were just missed.
holes_found.recommendation: Two trivial string substitutions, self-applyable in one diff: (a) `finding`: replace "Polaris is 0.74° from true pole" with "Polaris is 0.66° from true pole"; (b) `detail_verdict_text`: same substitution. Both occurrences are word-for-word identical so a single sed/replace on the substring works. Decider should also add to its self-apply checklist: "when propagating a numeric change, sweep ALL of {claim, finding, detail_*, tldr_*} fields, not just the field where the c-N hole was raised." Optionally route an ISS to capture the pattern so it stops slipping cycle-to-cycle.

holes_found.description: ERROR-BUDGET ARITHMETIC AMBIGUITY: detail_evidence post-patch reads "The combined error budget — Polaris's 0.66° polar offset (time-dependent), ~0.02–0.03° atmospheric refraction at mid-latitudes, and ±0.2–0.5° typical measurement uncertainty — yields a total uncertainty band of ±0.3–0.5°." The arithmetic does not reconcile cleanly: linear sum 0.66 + 0.03 + 0.5 = ±1.19°; RSS √(0.66² + 0.03² + 0.5²) ≈ ±0.83°; the stated ±0.3–0.5° band is roughly the time-averaged RMS (0.66/√2 ≈ 0.47°) plus measurement noise but the text does not say so. A defender re-running the addition gets a band 2–3× larger than the stated one. The argument survives at any of these widths (the dome's +0.27° claim sits inside every plausible band) but the un-reconciled arithmetic is a minor credibility ding. Was not raised in c3 (pre-existing field) but became more visible after the polar-offset value got smaller.
holes_found.recommendation: Either (a) add a clarifying qualifier — "yields a 1σ uncertainty band of ±0.3–0.5° after time-averaging the diurnal contribution", or (b) restate the dominant term: "Polaris's 0.66° polar offset alone exceeds the claimed +0.27° excess by 2.4×, before adding refraction and measurement uncertainty" (which is rhetorically stronger and avoids the band arithmetic entirely). Either fix is one-string.

advocate_mode.best_defense: PRED-NEW-001 is registered for high-latitude stations (Oslo, Helsinki, Edinburgh) and the test window is open ahead; the +0.27° Chapel Hill datapoint is an early signal, not the primary test. You are dunking on a preliminary observation while the actual prediction has not been measured yet. Also, the polar-offset value 0.66° is what you get if you compute 90° − declination at this epoch, but Polaris's diurnal circle envelope spans the full 1.32° peak-to-peak when sweeping over a sidereal day — so "0.74°" as a rough upper-bound on instantaneous offset over a many-hour observation window is not wrong, it is just a different convention. Your inconsistency between finding (0.74°) and detail (0.66°) reflects two valid framings, not an error.
advocate_mode.preemptive_recommendation: The "different conventions" defense for 0.74°-vs-0.66° is rhetorically possible but is undermined by the c3 hole 1 reasoning itself, which we accepted: "the parenthetical (2026) is factually wrong" — i.e., 0.74° came from the J2000 declination, not from a peak-to-peak envelope framing. The current text uses "~0.66° around the true pole" and "up to 0.66° above or below true north" — both clearly framed as instantaneous offset, not peak-to-peak. So the finding's 0.74° is unambiguously inconsistent with the detail's convention. The fix is the one-string substitution in holes_found[0]; defense_survives drops to 0 after that. The "early signal vs full test window" defense is partially valid but the Oslo coordinate-table contradiction inside the dome's own data is independent of any future measurement.

deeper_analysis: WIN-065.c4 is a verification with a meaningful coverage finding. The decider's commit (0606b13) executed 3 of 3 c3 holes substantively and propagated the polar-offset value through 7 occurrences across 3 fields (detail_evidence ×4, tldr_evidence ×2, tldr_verdict ×1) — but missed the same string in 2 additional fields (finding + detail_verdict_text) that are summary surfaces visible to readers who never expand the detail panel. This is the classic "patch the worked-on field, miss the parallel surface" pattern. The fix is trivial (2 one-string substitutions) but the gap is loud — the commit message itself enumerates the propagation scope ("4 detail_evidence + 2 tldr") in a way that signals the decider DID think about cross-field propagation but reached the wrong boundary. Additionally, the c3 hole 2 prose context (Cairo + Chapel Hill) was dropped in the patch, leaving "22 of 24" without an explanation of which 2 are outliers — and the same statistic in sections.json part6 was not updated. Four holes total: one major (finding + detail_verdict_text coverage), three minor (cross-page count, c3 hole 2 context, error-budget arithmetic). All four are self-applyable; no EXP needed. Verdict Refuted by Data holds unconditionally — none of the findings touch the substantive claim. Marking the batch as aborted-due-to-severity-upgrade per Step 8a procedure d (the decider classified queue_id 560 as verification-class but the actual coverage failure escalates to major; this is feedback for the dispatcher's class calibration — verification-class items should be safe to batch when the patch is complete-scope, and this one was not).
